heard: In 1859, telegraphs sent messages while completely unplugged from their batteries. On September 1, astronomer Richard Carrington saw two blinding white flashes on the sun. Only 17.6 hours later, a massive cloud of solar plasma slammed into Earth. Auroras glowed so bright that miners in the Rockies woke up to cook breakfast. Across the world, the magnetic storm induced high-voltage currents into the telegraph grid. Equipment sparked and set offices on fire as operators received electric shocks. Between Boston and Portland, operators realized they did not need their own batteries. They disconnected their equipment and successfully sent messages for about two hours using only the induced auroral current. That is how a solar storm kept the telegraphs talking without any batteries.
